hook_text: Six cranes, one table of rules agreed before anyone touched a switch. That is how you make judging fair.
clip_script: Before a single test, the class writes the rubric: criteria down the side, straight from the specifications. Lifts ten clips. Drops them in a second. Carries no foil. Reaches 150 up and 200 across. Stays standing. Bulb on when magnet on. Points across the top, and in every box words you can see, not feel: the back edge never lifts, not good stability. Then you go to another team's crane and run the tests yourself. Count. Measure. Watch the base. Three runs. Score what you saw, sign the sheet, write three things that worked and three to improve. Then your four minutes: brief, investigation, two sketches, drawing, chart, test numbers, one live lift. Say ferrous, not metal. Say more turns, more current, iron core. Say recycling saves ore, energy and water. Hold up the evidence as you speak.
visual_style: Whiteboard grid filling with criteria and points; a hand with a ruler at a crane; a signed sheet; six evidence documents held up in sequence.
mood: Fair-minded and proud, the class as a jury.
pacing: Rubric, boxes, test, score, feedback, present, three sayings, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the rubric before you judge a single crane.
